messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: spike detected - proxy 429/503 rate increased by 520% over 5m for route /v1/embeddings (primarily tenant: acme-corp). paging on-call. severity: P2

alex: I’m on it, paging phone now. checking the 429/503 heatmap and proxy queue length dashboards — zooming into region us-west1.

maria: seeing huge tail latency on proxy workers, queue depth at 95th pct is 18k reqs. looks like burst exhaustion plus backend overload. any recent deploys?

jordan: no deploys in last 2 hours from CICD. recent config change: new batching policy enabled for embeddings on dedicated runtime but should be safe.

alex: ok, first step — apply temporary traffic-shape to acme-corp to cap bursts and route non-critical requests to lower-priority pool. doing a small throttle to buy time.

sam: ready to run commands. suggested action from runbook: set tenant burst to 40, rps cap to 25 for affected tenant, enable failover-to-compat-model.

alex: running trafficctl now — attaching commands and output:
```
# limit tenant burst/rate (temporary)
trafficctl set-tenant-rate --tenant acme-corp --rps 25 --burst 40 --reason "live mitigation 429 spike"
trafficctl route --tenant acme-corp --pool low-priority --prob 0.4
```

sam: trafficctl: accepted, config push id=cfg-20240708-1143, routing prob change applied.

incident-bot: snapshot: 1m 429 rate before action: 128/s, after action (5m): 42/s. 503s reduced from 18/s -> 6/s.

nina: notifying CS and account lead for acme-corp. preparing customer message: short note + ETA for mitigation.

customer-success-bot: Draft to customer sent to #customer-success for review: "We observed elevated request errors and implemented temporary rate shaping to reduce errors. We will follow up with timeline and root cause."

maria: still seeing some slow tail but queue depth trending down. backend model nodes showing heavy KV cache churn; might be cache eviction thrash under bursty keys from acme corp.

jordan: can we disable the preview feature that fans out extra requests? that will reduce overall qps by ~12%.

alex: yep, toggle feature flag for acme-corp to off — doing via ffctl.

alex: ```
ffctl set --flag preview-autocomplete --tenant acme-corp --value false --reason "reduce fanout during mitigation"
```

sam: ffctl OK. feature flag change deployed to edge in ~10s.

incident-bot: metric update: 429s now 18/s, 503s 3/s. latency p95 back to baseline ≈220ms.

nina: good, sending status update to account team: "mitigation in place, error rates dropped by ~85%, monitoring for stability, will open incident with timeline and follow-ups."

alex: handing off to @jordan for next 2 hours to watch dashboards and continue customer comms. leaving notes:
- mitigation commands applied (trafficctl cfg-20240708-1143)
- feature flag preview-autocomplete disabled for acme-corp
- follow up: collect sampling traces for cache churn, check model KV eviction logs, assess need for permanent shaping or capacity bump

jordan: ack. will monitor, will escalate if 429/503 > 10/s sustained for >10m. adding to oncall checklist and pinging infra to check dedicated model pool memory pressure.

maria: as a follow-up task: run auto-batcher revert test on staging to reproduce KV churn; assign to eng-ml.

alex: creating incident in pagerduty with summary and mitigation steps, tagging eng-ml and infra. incident id PD-987654.

incident-bot: PD-987654 created by alex. severity set to P2, responders: eng-oncall, eng-ml, infra, customer-success.

sam: quick note for post-incident: consider adding a targeted per-tenant token-bucket limiter in edge proxy that prevents large transient bursts from filling long-tail queues. file follow-up ticket in backlog.

jordan: observed slight uptick in 429 at 1728456950 but subsided after small routing tweak. dashboards stable now.

nina: customer update sent: "We implemented traffic shaping and feature toggles which reduced error rates. We’ll follow with a post-incident report and next steps for capacity/limits."

alex: closing loop for now — mitigation successful, handing to the oncall runbook for scheduled checks. please add any additional notes here so I can include them in the postmortem.

maria: note: we should add a SLO alert that fires earlier on proxy queue depth (current alert triggers too late). ticket created: INF-3241.

jordan: will own follow-up to prototype per-tenant soft-limiter (spike absorb). assigning to eng-runtime.

incident-bot: thread closed to active paging at 1728457030 — status: mitigated, monitoring.
